Behind the Rise of the Front National

The trend has been young French people buying into the grandeur of right-wing populism that the Front National offers. While not explicitly fascist, fascist wings are present within the party. Bigotry and cultism are at the foundation of the party.

It heralds itself as a party for the working class, but opposes systems of the working class e.g. trade unions. The working class is willing to vote against their interests. This support isn't a case of Stockholm syndrome. It is out of fear of migrant workers, even in towns where there are few of these migrants workers.

Meanwhile, the left walks through the changing political climate unscathed. The phenomenon is limited to those that had voted to the right anyway, and it just so happens that many that may vote for their interests are unable to.

The rise of the Front National is concerning, as a large number of workers in France are immigrants. The threat is two-fold. One, in the trend of effective propaganda for the Front National and two, the inability of the right to keep from devouring themselves. Without the migrant workers having a say, and having the ability to protect their interests the two issues will exacerbate one another.
